title: The Mouse Deer and the High Mango
summary: The mouse deer cannot reach the ripe mango at the top of the tree, so it says the mango must be sour. Is that really true?
moral: Do not belittle something just because you cannot reach it. Admit your limits, then ask for help.
pages: That afternoon the mouse deer's stomach was rumbling. Suddenly its eyes fell on a very tall mango tree. Its fruit was ripe golden yellow, hanging at the tips of the branches. 'Wow, it must be so sweet!' it said.
The mouse deer took a run-up and leapt as high as it could. Hop! But the mango was still too high. It tried again, hop! Still not enough.
Again and again the mouse deer leapt, until it was out of breath and its legs ached. It sat down under the tree, gazing at the tempting mangoes. 'Oh, so high...'
Annoyed, the mouse deer stood up and said, 'Ah, who needs that mango? It must be sour and tasteless. I would rather leave!' It walked away pretending not to care.
A bird landed on a branch and pecked at the mango. 'Hmm, so sweet and fresh!' it said cheerfully. The mouse deer, hearing from afar, was stunned and ashamed, for its words had turned out to be wrong.

The mouse deer took a breath and said honestly, 'Friends, I cannot reach that mango. Can Elephant help me?' The elephant, passing by, smiled, then reached out its long trunk and picked several mangoes.

The mouse deer, the elephant, and the bird ate the sweet mangoes together. The mouse deer learned that admitting your limits is not shameful, and that asking for help lets us reach what we cannot take by ourselves. The end.
